fixed: 2026-09-25, before any outcome of these runs; retrospective on the previously exposed 225-task bank
protocol: Retrospective strengthening study for the WCL letter, fixed 2026-09-25 before any outcome.
Scope. Same 225 recorded task pairs, 450 responses (truncations kept), CARROT frozen
paired-quality predictions and charged prediction time, causal FIFO/residual wait
estimator, shared downlink scheduler, twelve conditions, twenty paired traffic seeds,
achieved cost L + beta*shortfall + 1000*fees. No provider calls, no new tasks, no
retraining, no Fresh450 access. Everything below is retrospective on a previously
exposed bank; nothing here is independent confirmation.
Question 1 (derived workload coefficient, "FPI"). The workload term
kappa*E[((w+S)^2-w^2)/2] has exactly the form of the first-policy-iteration admission
cost for FCFS M/G/1 queues, whose relative value is lambda*u^2/(2(1-rho)) (Krishnan
1990; Hyytia, Penttinen, Aalto 2012). Under proportional (Bernoulli) splitting of the
configured offered load, each slot of route m has utilisation rho and arrival rate
rho/mbar_m, where mbar_m = MIX @ arrival_mu[:,m] is the same calibration service time
used to normalise arrivals. FPI uses kappa_m = rho/((1-rho)*mbar_m) per route, no
fitted constant. It is otherwise CARROT-Queue. A previous coefficient-free M/M/c
externality (erlang_externality_v1) failed at high load; that failure stays reported.
Gate (declared now): FPI is described as a derived replacement for kappa=0.5 only if
its paired 95% t interval versus CARROT-Queue has upper bound <= 0 in the equal-12
scope AND its mean is not higher than CARROT-Queue at any configured load in the load
sweep. Otherwise report it as a failed/partial candidate and keep kappa=0.5 as the
paper's controller.
Question 2 (weight robustness). Controller beta in {4,8,12,16,24,36} for CARROT-Queue,
FPI, Shortfall-Queue, Utility-Queue on all 12x20 paths. Report mean delay, p95 delay,
quality, shortfall, fees for every point (trade-off curves). Also evaluate every run
at achieved beta=12: the best Utility/Shortfall controller beta chosen IN HINDSIGHT on
the evaluation paths is a baseline-favouring comparison; our methods keep beta=12.
Question 3 (load). rho in {0.35,0.5,0.65,0.8,0.9}, primary radio: Intrinsic,
Shortfall, Utility, CARROT-Queue (kappa .5), FPI, kappa in {0.25,1,2}.
Question 4 (kappa sensitivity). kappa in {0.125,0.25,1,2} on 12x20 (0 and .5 exist).
Question 5 (serial edge). The local concurrency probe showed no parallel speed-up.
Rerun with one edge slot (cloud four), arrival normalised by the resulting capacity,
rho in {0.5,0.65,0.8}: Intrinsic, Shortfall, Utility, CARROT-Queue, FPI.
Question 6 (task-bank sensitivity of the headline). The same 200 banks as the paper
(master seed 2026092301, traffic seeds 23924000/1, all 12 conditions): CARROT-Queue,
FPI, Shortfall-Queue, Utility-Queue. Percentile 2.5/97.5 of the equal-12 difference.
References rows. Always-edge and Always-cloud (no predictor, no charged prediction
time). Oracle-quality Queue: realized route qualities replace CARROT predictions with
CARROT prediction charges retained (value-of-information bound, not deployable).
CARROT-Queue-Radio (release correction) and FPI-Radio.
Parity. CARROT-Queue and CARROT-Release reproduce all archived choice hashes on 12x20;
Utility/Shortfall at beta=12 and Intrinsic at rho=.65 reproduce archived hashes.
Report every run including unfavourable ones. No outcome-based dropping of conditions.

extension_v1_5.fixed: 2026-09-25, before any outcome of these runs
protocol: Extension of the value-of-information study, fixed 2026-09-25 before any outcome of these runs.
Same bank, predictors, charges, scheduler, and achieved cost as protocol.txt. Retrospective.
No gate; both extensions are descriptive and every run is reported.
E1 (payload). Primary radio (100 kHz), rho 0.65, four edge slots. Response bytes scaled by
payload_scale in {1, 2, 4, 8, 12} (nominal airtime load 0.12 ... 1.43). This is a synthetic
stand-in for larger (e.g. multimodal) outputs: chunk timing, quality, fees, and RPC durations
are unchanged; only transmitted bits scale. Methods: CARROT-Queue, CARROT-Radio, Mean-Queue,
Mean-Radio, Intrinsic (CARROT). 20 seeds. Parity: scale 1 reproduces archived CARROT-Queue,
CARROT-Radio, Mean (strengthening 'mean') and Mean-Radio ('mean_release') choice hashes.
E2 (serial edge). All 12 conditions x 20 seeds with one edge slot (cloud four), arrival
normalised by the resulting capacity. Methods: Intrinsic, Utility-Queue, Shortfall-Queue,
CARROT-Queue, FPI-Queue, CARROT-Radio, Oracle-Queue, Always-cloud, Mean-Queue, Mean-Radio.
Always-edge is not run: its offered load exceeds one-slot edge capacity in every condition.
Report beside the four-slot results in the manuscript table.

radio_diagnostic_v1_6.fixed: 2026-09-25, before any outcome of these runs
protocol: Radio decision diagnostic, fixed 2026-09-25 before any outcome of these runs. Descriptive, no gate.
Question: why does the radio term help the Mean predictor but not CARROT (manuscript Fig. 2(c))?
Paths: predictors {CARROT (cq/cq_release), Mean (mean_cq/mean_release)} x settings {payload 1, 4, 8, 12
at 100 kHz; 10 kHz at payload 1} x 20 seeds x {Queue, Radio} = 400 paths. Same controllers as v1.4-v1.5;
each Queue/Radio pair shares arrivals, targets, channel, and charges.
Per pair, over post-warmup requests:
- flip rate: fraction whose route differs between Radio and Queue; share of flips toward the cloud;
- for flipped requests: realized change in beta*shortfall + gamma*fee (the route's recorded response),
and the change predicted by the controller's own quality estimate (beta*predicted shortfall);
- total change in mean weighted cost, split into the quality+fee part (sum over flipped requests / n)
and the remainder (delay, including effects on other requests).
Report every setting and both predictors. Flips are defined against the Queue path of the same seed;
because trajectories diverge after the first flip, this is a paired descriptive decomposition, not a
causal per-decision effect.
